name: Stock Replacement with Deep ITM LEAPS
summary: Sell (or never buy) the shares and hold a single deep ITM long-dated call instead, freeing capital and capping downside at the premium.

greeks.theta: negative but small per day on a LEAPS

when_to_use: Bullish long-horizon view, want to free up capital, and IV Rank is LOW (<= 30) so the long vega is cheap. Also used to keep exposure while removing the capital drag of shares in a $50k account.
entry_rules: Delta in [0.80, 0.90]; extrinsic <= 8% of premium paid.
Require IV Rank <= 35 - never buy long vega when IV is rich.
Require premium <= 35% of the cost of 100 shares.
Require LEAPS OI >= 100 and spread <= 5% of mid.
Avoid underlyings with dividend yield > 3% (the long call forgoes dividends and is priced accordingly).
management_rules: Roll out when DTE < 120 or delta < 0.65.
Take profit in line with the share plan; optionally convert to a PMCC by selling 30-45 DTE calls against it once the position is up 20%.
Cut if the position loses 50% of premium.
exit_rules: HARD: close before expiration - an ITM long call auto-exercises at $0.01 ITM under OCC exercise-by-exception and delivers 100 long shares requiring full cash/margin. Close by 15:30 ET on expiration day at the latest.
Close if delta < 0.50 (it has become a speculative option, not a stock substitute).
assignment_risk: No short leg, so no assignment risk. The mirror risk is unwanted EXERCISE: the long call will be auto-exercised if ITM at expiry, converting a $3,000 option into a $40,000 share purchase. That must be blocked by closing early.
buying_power: Premium paid, in full (long options are never marginable).
liquidity_needs: LEAPS liquidity is the constraint; mega-caps and large ETFs only.
common_mistakes: Buying when IV is high; picking too low a delta and getting a decaying lottery ticket; forgetting the auto-exercise at expiration.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable - the whole point is long duration.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
